messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @channel — elevated inference error rate (5xx) and tail latency spike in AWS region usw1a for the past ~3m. Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings. Initial signal from probe cluster.

alex (oncall): ack, I'm looking. Any customer impact yet?

mina (sre): seeing increased gRPC resets from a subset of hosts in usw1a, RX/TX counters show packet drops on eth0. Application logs show kvcache misses spike.

raj (infra): AWS console: a handful of c5n/g5 instances in subnet-3 are showing network interface RxErrors and ENI detach/reattach events. No AZ-wide outage reported but localized host degradation.

lee (support): we have two customers reporting increased latencies and a small uptick in error retries. Notified customer success.

mina (sre): rolling `kubectl get pods -o wide` shows pods on node-198 and node-203 have >200ms p95 latency for initial RPCs. KV cache warmups failing, so requests are doing full forward passes.

alex (oncall): plan: 1) divert new traffic off problematic hosts via proxy redispatch 2) trigger autoscale to warm healthy hosts in other AZs/region 3) start draining affected nodes. Who owns redispatch?

raj (infra): ops-bot: run redispatch tag=usw1a avoid_nodes=node-198,node-203 -> ops-bot: command accepted, updating L4 proxy weight tables. (reaction :white_check_mark:)

ops-bot: redispatch complete. Estimated traffic shift ~40% in 60s. Monitoring.

mina (sre): initiating node drain for node-198 and node-203: `kubectl drain node-198 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — pods re-scheduled to other nodes in same AZ first. If capacity insufficient we'll expand to cross-AZ.

alex (oncall): enable cross-AZ spillover now to speed recovery. ops-bot: set steering_policy=allow-cross-az for route inference.default

ops-bot: steering_policy updated. Cross-AZ spillover enabled.

mina (sre): autoscaler triggered +3 instances in usw1b and +2 in eu-west-1 as part of cross-AZ fallback. New hosts reporting healthy on probe checks.

lee (support): sending short customer note: "We're seeing elevated latency in US-WEST that may cause retries/errors for a subset of requests. We are actively mitigating and will update in 30m."

raj (infra): also observed increased DNS resolution latency for resolver endpoint srv-resolver.usw1a — TTLs look normal but latency to resolver endpoints up ~120ms. Might be contributing to controlplane retries.

mina (sre): temporarily switching endpoints for model-fetch and healthchecks to resolver fallback pool — patching config: `MODEL_FETCH_DAEMON_RESOLVERS=[srv-resolver-fallback-1, srv-resolver-fallback-2]`

alex (oncall): good. Any sign this will be long-running?

raj (infra): AWS support case opened (case# 123456789). They see transient NIC errors on 5 EC2 instances in the subnet; they've flagged it as potential underlying host NIC driver flakiness. ETA unknown.

mina (sre): mitigation status: redispatch + cross-AZ spillover reduced p95 latency from 950ms -> 220ms over 8 minutes. Error rate down 65%. KVCACHE miss rate back to baseline on new hosts.

lee (support): customers acknowledged, some ask for ETA. We're sharing that we've moved traffic and are awaiting AWS host-level remediation.

alex (oncall): ok plan for next 60m: continue draining affected nodes, keep cross-AZ spillover, monitor cost/latency tradeoff, update customers at +30m. If AWS doesn't clear hosts in 45m, trigger broader region failover per runbook. Assignments: alex = incident lead, mina = mitigation owner, raj = infra liaison, lee = customer comms.

mina (sre): note: disable rolling restarts on deployments touching kvcache until drains finish to avoid cache churn.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1482, severity=high, owner=alex.

alex (oncall): handing off to night SRE on 1749996200 (30m). Mina please keep monitoring and update thread.

mina (sre): will do, posting small probe metrics every 5m. Current p95=210ms, 5xx rate=0.8% (down from 2.4%).

lee (support): customer update posted to affected accounts.

alex (oncall): :thumbsup: — handing off to oncall-north at 1749996200. If regression, page oncall-primary.

ops-bot: handoff acknowledged to oncall-north.

mina (sre): follow-up at 1749997800: AWS reports remediation applied to underlying hosts; reattach/evict events stopped. Drain completed, pods stabilized. p95=180ms, 5xx=0.3%. Suggest closing incident after 1h of steady state.

lee (support): will send final customer note once we hit 1h steady.

alex (oncall): closing plan accepted. Good work.
